headline: Yields near two-decade highs and Iran tensions keep risk appetite cautious
body: Equities are trying to stabilize Friday after Thursday's sharp risk-off session, when the Dow shed nearly 700 points (-1.3%), the S&P 500 fell 0.8%, and the Nasdaq dropped about 1%. Futures point to a modest rebound -- Dow futures up roughly 0.3%, Nasdaq futures up roughly 0.6% -- but the bounce reads more like relief than conviction. The proximate pressure is a bond market that keeps grinding to new multi-decade highs: the 10-year Treasury yield has climbed to around 4.7% and the 30-year has touched levels last seen in 2007, weighing on capital-intensive AI and growth names. Walmart compounded the mood, sliding about 9% despite beating on both earnings and revenue, after guidance flagged slowing U.S. comparable-sales growth -- a result some are reading as an early crack in consumer resilience rather than pure company-specific noise.

Layered on top is a geopolitical thread: the administration's declared 'economic warfare' campaign against Iran pushed Brent crude up more than 2% toward $94 a barrel, feeding the same inflation worries already unsettling the bond market. A Treasury move to roughly double its longer-dated debt buybacks briefly eased yields midweek, but that relief evaporated within a day, suggesting the pressure is more structural -- heavy issuance, deficit concerns, AI-linked corporate debt supply -- than purely sentiment-driven, which tends to unsettle markets more. Retail and social chatter today reads thinner and less directional than the macro headlines; the more concrete signal is elevated interest in semiconductor and AI-adjacent names, consistent with a tape still fixated on rates rather than a fresh retail-driven narrative.
